'''Christopher McLean Skinner'''  (born 4 June 1972) is an American [[mathematician]] and professor at [[Princeton University]]. He works in [[algebraic number theory]] and arithmetic aspects of the [[Langlands program]].

==Early life and education==
Skinner was born on 4 June 1972, in [[Little Rock]], Arkansas.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=http://math.caltech.edu/events/Skinner%20CV.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120803072357/http://math.caltech.edu/events/Skinner%20CV.pdf |archive-date=3 August 2012 |title=Curriculum Vitae |website=Christopher Skinner}}</ref> Skinner graduated with a B.A. from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1993.<ref name="CV"/> He received a Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 1997 under the supervision of [[Andrew Wiles]].<ref name="CV"/>

== Career ==
Skinner was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1997 to 2000.<ref name="CV"/> He was then an associate professor of mathematics at the University of Michigan from 2000 to 2004, and then a full professor from 2004 to 2006.<ref name="CV"/> He became a professor of mathematics at [[Princeton University]] in 2006.<ref name="CV"/>

==Research==
Skinner and Wiles proved [[Modularity theorem#Generalizations|modularity]] results for residually reducible [[Galois representation]]s in joint work.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://www.numdam.org/article/PMIHES_1999__89__5_0.pdf |first1=Christopher |last1=Skinner |first2=Andrew |last2=Wiles |author2-link=Andrew Wiles |title=Residually reductible representations and modular forms |journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]] |year=1999 |volume=89 |pages=5–126 |doi=10.1007/BF02698855 }}</ref>

Skinner and [[Eric Urban]] proved many cases of [[Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory|Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture]]s for a large class of [[modular form]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Urban|first1=Eric|last2=Skinner|first2=Christopher|date=2014-01-01|title=The Iwasawa Main Conjectures for GL2|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|volume=195|issue=1|pages=1–277|doi=10.1007/s00222-013-0448-1|issn=1432-1297|bibcode=2014InMat.195....1S|s2cid=120848645}}</ref> As a consequence, for a [[modular elliptic curve]] over the [[rational number]]s, they prove that the vanishing of the [[Hasse–Weil L-function|Hasse–Weil ''L''-function]] ''L''(''E'',&nbsp;''s'') of ''E'' at ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 implies that the p-adic [[Selmer group]] of ''E'' is infinite. Combined with theorems of [[Benedict Gross|Gross]]–[[Don Zagier|Zagier]] and [[Victor Kolyvagin|Kolyvagin]], this gave a conditional proof (on the [[Tate–Shafarevich conjecture]]) of the conjecture that ''E'' has infinitely many rational points if and only if ''L''(''E'',&nbsp;1) =  0, a (weak) form of the [[Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]]. These results were used by [[Manjul Bhargava]], Skinner, and [[Wei Zhang (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]] to prove that a positive proportion of elliptic curves satisfy the [[Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Bhargava|first1=Manjul|last2=Skinner|first2=Christopher|last3=Zhang|first3=Wei|date=2014-07-07|title=A majority of elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ satisfy the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture|eprint=1407.1826|class=math.NT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mattbaker.blog/2014/03/10/the-bsd-conjecture-is-true-for-most-elliptic-curves/|title=The BSD conjecture is true for most elliptic curves|last=Baker|first=Matt|date=2014-03-10|website=Matt Baker's Math Blog|language=en|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Skinner was a [[Packard Foundation]] Fellow from 2001 to 2006<ref name="CV"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.packard.org/what-we-fund/science/packard-fellowships-for-science-and-engineering/fellowship-directory/skinner-christopher-m/|title=Skinner, Christopher M.|website=The David and Lucile Packard Foundation|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref> and a [[Sloan Research Fellow]] from 2001 to 2002.<ref name="CV"/> He was named an inaugural [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/home/page/|title=American Mathematical Society|website=ams.org|language=en|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref> In 2015, he was named a [[Simons Investigator]] in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.princeton.edu/news/2015/07/10/faculty-award-skinner-named-simons-investigator-mathematics|title=FACULTY AWARD: Skinner named Simons Investigator in Mathematics|publisher=Princeton University|language=en|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-physical-sciences/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-awardees/|title=Simons Investigators|website=Simons Foundation|date=10 July 2018|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref>

He was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Madrid in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=skinner|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=mathunion.org|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref>
